name: kartseek-super-app
description: KARTSEEK — Multi-vertical Super App monorepo (Web · API · Mobile)

scripts.infra:up: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d && npm run kafka:topics
scripts.nginx:reload: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml exec nginx nginx -s reload
scripts.nginx:test: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml exec nginx nginx -t
scripts.nginx:certs: mkdir -p infra/nginx/ssl && docker run --rm -v ./infra/nginx/ssl:/ssl alpine/openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout /ssl/kartseek.key -out /ssl/kartseek.crt -subj /C=GB/ST=London/L=London/O=KARTSEEK/OU=Engineering/CN=localhost -addext subjectAltName=DNS:localhost,DNS:kartseek.local,IP:127.0.0.1
scripts.db:seed: npm run db:seed:grocery && npm run db:seed:marketplace && npm run db:seed:restaurant && npm run db:seed:pharmacy

_comment_typeorm: Declared at the root on purpose, alongside the override. @nestjs/typeorm@11 lists typeorm as a peer with range '^0.3.0 || ^1.0.0-dev', so npm auto-installed the highest match (1.1.0) and hoisted it. TypeORM 1.x dropped the array forms of `select` and `relations` that this codebase uses in dozens of places, so every workspace package had to pin ^0.3.31 to get a nested copy. Pinning the hoisted version here means one typeorm for the whole repo and no per-module workaround.
_comment_nest_core_override: @nestjs/typeorm and @nestjs/mongoose peer on ^10 || ^11 || ^12, and npm satisfied that with a leftover 11.x while every workspace resolved 12. Two copies of @nestjs/core in one tree is the dual-package hazard: an HttpException built against one is not instanceof the other, so the gateway's exception filter would classify a real HttpException as an unknown error and answer 500. Pinned to one version rather than trusting hoisting.
_comment_nest_root_pin: Declared at the root on purpose. Nothing here imports Nest — these exist to pin one version for the whole tree. @nestjs/typeorm and @nestjs/mongoose peer on ^10 || ^11 || ^12, and npm satisfied that by hoisting an 11.x to the root while the workspaces resolved 12. The v12 packages import '@nestjs/common/internal', a subpath that 11.x does not export, so every build that reached the hoisted copy failed with 'Can't resolve @nestjs/common/internal'. `overrides` did not fix this — npm reported 'up to date' through --force and after clearing the install-state cache. A direct dependency outranks a peer-satisfied hoist, which does. @nestjs/websockets is here for the same reason: @nestjs/core lazily requires '@nestjs/websockets/socket-module.js', webpack resolves that statically, and only apps/api declared it — so a module backend building against the root core could not find it. Under Nest 11 it happened to be hoisted; that is not something to rely on.
